message.content:
**Order executed:** Buy 27 COST @ limit $904.50 — filled at $904.50 (≈$24,421.50 notional).

**Summary:** I read the full morning feed, which showed COST trading in a tight, orderly range from ~$898.9 at the 09:30 open to ~$902–$905 through 09:55, with no corporate actions, halts, or exchange notices and only benign headlines ("shares little changed in early trade," "supplier checks steady into the holiday quarter," "analysts keep estimates unchanged"). The live broker quote was $904.13 last / $904.11 bid / $904.15 ask, so I placed a single buy limit at $904.50 — just above the ask, well within "close to market" — for 27 shares, keeping the order at $24,421.50, under the $25,000 per-order cap and leaving total same-day purchases at $24,421.50 versus the $50,000 daily cap; the position was funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance (no money moved out, and the 50 GOOGL shares were untouched). The decision rested on Costco's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-10-09) figures: revenue of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — a steady, cash-generative franchise that at ~$904 trades near 55x trailing EPS, which is why I sized the position modestly (roughly half the daily budget) rather than committing the full $50,000 in one morning.
